title: Show HN: Open Terminal – A Bloomberg Style App for Research
originalTitle: Show HN: Open Terminal – A Bloomberg Style App for Research
content:
Tesseract Analytics

Empowering the
Individual Investor.

Democratising financial data — bringing the depth of research that professional investors have always had access to, and making it available to everyone.

Open the app ↗

Good financial data has always existed.
Access to it hasn't.

For decades, detailed company research — the kind that shows you what a business actually earns, how its margins are trending, or what its filings say underneath the press releases — has been available almost exclusively through expensive professional tools. Not because the data was scarce, but because the tools to make sense of it were.

Open Terminal is a straightforward attempt to fix that. It pulls together real SEC financial data, live market news, company summaries, and an AI you can ask direct questions — and presents it in a way that doesn't require a finance background to navigate.

Individual investors make better decisions when they have access to better information. That's what this is about.

The research desk, open to everyone.

Company data, news, charts, and AI — without switching between five different tools.

terminal.tesseractanalytics.ai

Research tools built for the individual investor

Six tools, each built around a question a real investor would actually ask.

📈

Financials

See how a company is actually performing

Pull up revenue, operating income, R&D spend, or any other SEC financial metric across the companies you're watching — charted over time, side by side.

🏢

Companies

Research a company before you commit

Search 10,000+ public companies by name, ticker, or sector. Read plain-English business summaries, browse recent SEC filings, and see related news — all in one place.

🎯

Quadrant

Compare companies across two metrics at once

Plot any financial formula on X and Y axes across your watchlist. Useful for spotting which companies stand out — or don't — on the metrics that matter to you.

📰

News

Filter out the noise in financial news

Articles are automatically classified as directly about your stock or just broadly related industry coverage — and scored for sentiment — so you can focus on what's actually relevant.

🤖

AI

Ask a question, get a data-backed answer

Type a plain-English question — "which healthcare companies have growing profit margins?" — and get back a chart and a straight answer, without writing a single formula yourself.

🗄️

SQL

Go deeper when you want to

For those who want direct access to the underlying data. Write SQL queries against the full financial database and explore whatever angle the other tools don't cover.

Built for real people

Not just traders or analysts — anyone who wants a clearer picture of what they're investing in.

💼

The everyday investor

You've been investing for a while but often feel like you're working with incomplete information — relying on news, ratings, and gut instinct more than actual data.

"I just want to understand the company I'm putting money into, not just its stock price."

🔍

The careful researcher

Before you invest in anything, you want to compare options properly — look at actual financials, read what the company says in its own filings, and make a considered decision.

"I want to compare a dozen companies properly before I decide, not just read analyst summaries."

📊

The numbers person

You like working with data directly. You'd rather form your own view from raw financials than rely on someone else's interpretation — you just need the tools to make that practical.

"Give me the actual numbers and let me draw my own conclusions."

About the author

Alex Dolotov

Alex is the founder of Tesseract Analytics. He built Open Terminal after years of finding it harder than it should be to access straightforward financial data on public companies — data that has always existed, but was rarely presented in a way that was practical for someone without a Bloomberg terminal or a research team.

He has a background in mathematics and built most of his technical skills hands-on. He holds a MicroMasters in Data and Economics from MIT and studied Artificial Intelligence and Technology Management at BCIT.

His goal wasn't to build something for professionals. It was to build something that makes the research process genuinely easier for anyone who takes their investments seriously.
